chunks: From him, from his father, transmitted as a continuous chain, he said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not take anyone other than Allah as a confidant, so that you do not cease to be believers. For every reason, lineage, kinship, confidant, innovation, and doubt will be cut off and fade away, just as the dust that is upon a solid rock fades away when the abundant rain strikes it, except for what has been established by the Quran.'

key_terms.سَبَب: Reason, cause, or means of support

ai.seo_question: What does it mean to take Allah as the only Wali (confidant/guardian) according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Ja'far (as) warns against relying on created intermediaries for spiritual or worldly support, emphasizing that all human ties—kinship, lineage, and authority—are transient and will dissolve like dust washed from a solid rock by rain. This metaphor underscores the fragility of worldly dependencies, with the Quran serving as the sole enduring anchor for believers. The hadith highlights the Shia concept of *Tawhid* in practice, where ultimate reliance (*Waliyyah*) belongs exclusively to Allah, while acknowledging that Quranic institutions remain valid exceptions.
